rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A trigonometric equation is solved in two moves: **reduce, then generalise**. Reduce to one function of one angle (factor quadratics in sin/cos; use cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1, sin² + cos² = 1, sum→product). Then apply the **general value theorems**: sin θ = sin α ⟹ **θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα** (sine mirrors about π/2), cos θ = cos α ⟹ **θ = 2nπ ± α** (cosine is even), tan θ = tan α ⟹ **θ = nπ + α** (tangent just repeats); squared…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - sin θ = sin α ⟹ θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα; cos θ = cos α ⟹ θ = 2nπ ± α; tan θ = tan α ⟹ θ = nπ + α - sin²θ = sin²α ⟹ θ = nπ ± α (likewise cos², tan²) - sin θ = 0 ⟹ θ = nπ; cos θ = 0 ⟹ θ = (2n+1)π/2; sin θ = 1 ⟹ θ = 2nπ + π/2

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024 (2sin^2 th - sin th - 1 = 0), NEB 2022 (cos 2th = cos th) — assigned to this row. NEB 2023's inverse-value item bridges to the next row.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "sin th = sin a iff th = n*pi + (-1)^n a; cos th = cos a iff th = 2n*pi +- a; tan th = tan a iff th = n*pi + a."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Filter, don't forget*** — sin th = -1/2 has infinitely many solutions; the interval [0, 2pi] keeps exactly two of them (7pi/6 and 11pi/6) plus none from the sin = 1 branch.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The three families encode each function's symmetry: sine mirrors about pi/2 ((-1)^n), cosine is even (+-), tangent just repeats (n*pi).  ·  General value theorems: sin th = sin a => th = n*pi + (-1)^n a; cos th = cos a => th = 2n*pi +- a; tan th = tan a => th = n*pi + a (radians). Squared versions all give th = n*pi +- a. Standard families: sin th = 0 => n*pi; cos th = 0 => (2n+1)pi/2; sin th = 1 => 2n*pi + pi/2; cos th = 1 => 2n*pi.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — From Solutions to Families A trigonometric **equation** is true for *some* angles; the job is to describe **all** of them. The key theorem: if sin θ = sin α (or cos θ = cos α, tan θ = tan α), then θ belongs to a **general value family** — infinitely many angles spaced by the function's period, plus a reflection about the axis.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The general value theorems - **Theorem (sine):** sin θ = sin α ⟺ **θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα**, n ∈ ℤ. - **Theorem (cosine):** cos θ = cos α ⟺ **θ = 2nπ ± α**, n ∈ ℤ. - **Theorem (tangent):** tan θ = tan α ⟺ **θ = nπ + α**, n ∈ ℤ (α in radians).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Factor first (2sin^2 - sin - 1 = (2sin+1)(sin-1)). Principal value in [-pi/2, pi/2] for sin/tan, [0, pi] for cos. Filter n = 0, 1, 2 into the interval. Squared equation: th = n*pi +- a for all three functions.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve: 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. (4m)** — **Factorise:** treat as a quadratic in sin θ: 2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = **(2sinθ + 1)(sinθ − 1) = 0**, so sin θ = 1 or sin θ = −1/2. **Case sin θ = 1:** principal value α = π/2, so θ = 2nπ + π/2; inside [0, 2π] this gives **θ = π/2** only.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Solve: cos 2θ = cos θ. (4m)** — **Reduce to one function:** cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1, so the equation becomes 2cos²θ − 1 = cos θ, i.e. **2cos²θ − cosθ − 1 = 0**. **Factorise:** (2cosθ + 1)(cosθ − 1) = 0, giving cos θ = 1 or cos θ = −1/2. **Case cos θ = 1:** principal value α = 0, so θ = **2nπ**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: List every solution inside the interval explicitly - the filter step carries marks even when the family is right.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every trig equation has either no solution or infinitely many; the general value family is how "infinitely many" is written down.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Solve for x, 0° < x < 90°: 3sin²x − 4cos²x + 1 = 0.** — Replace cos²x = 1 − sin²x: 3sin²x − 4(1 − sin²x) + 1 = 0 ⟹ **7sin²x − 3 = 0** ⟹ sin²x = 3/7 ⟹ **sin x = √(3/7)** (positive, since 0° < x < 90°). Hence **x = sin⁻¹√(3/7) ≈ 40.9°**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **General value** | The full family of solutions of a trig equation | sin θ = 1/2 ⟹ θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6) | | **Principal value** | The representative solution in the standard branch | π/6 for sin θ = 1/2 | | **Period** | Smallest T with f(θ + T) = f(θ): π for tan, 2π for sin/cos | controls…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the families look different - Sine is symmetric about π/2 (its mirror), so solutions alternate sides — captured by the (−1)ⁿ factor. Cosine is even (symmetric about 0), so solutions come in ± pairs. Tangent repeats with period π and has no mirror — hence the plain nπ + α.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **General values at a glance** | Equation | General solution | Spacing | |---|---|---| | sin θ = sin α | θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα | alternates | | cos θ = cos α | θ = 2nπ ± α | paired | | tan θ = tan α | θ = nπ + α | uniform | | sin²θ = sin²α | θ = nπ ± α | paired | | cos²θ = cos²α | θ = nπ ± α | paired | | tan²θ = tan²α | θ = nπ ± α | paired |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Solve 2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π.  ·  Solve cos 2θ = cos θ and write the general solution.  ·  State the general values of sin θ = sin α and tan θ = tan α with one-line proofs.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Degrees vs radians:** the general-value theorems are stated in **radians** — convert the interval before filtering.  ·  **(−1)ⁿ belongs to sine only:** writing θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα for cosine is a signature error; cosine uses 2nπ ± α.  ·  **Interval endpoints:** "0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π" includes both ends — test n values that land exactly on 0 or 2π.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve: 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. (4m)** — Factor: **2sin²θ − sinθ − 1 = (2sinθ + 1)(sinθ − 1) = 0**. Case 1: **sin θ = 1** ⟹ principal α = π/2 ⟹ θ = 2nπ + π/2; inside [0, 2π]: **θ = π/2** (n = 0) and θ = 5π/2 is outside.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): Solve: cos 2θ = cos θ. (4m)** — Use **cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1**: 2cos²θ − 1 = cos θ ⟹ **2cos²θ − cos θ − 1 = 0** ⟹ (2cos θ + 1)(cos θ − 1) = 0. Case 1: **cos θ = 1** ⟹ α = 0 ⟹ θ = 2nπ. Case 2: **cos θ = −1/2** ⟹ α = 2π/3 ⟹ θ = 2nπ ± 2π/3. General solution: **θ = 2nπ or θ = 2nπ ± 2π/3**, n ∈ ℤ.…  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): Find cos⁻¹(√3/2) + sin⁻¹(1/2). (2m)** — Principal values: **cos⁻¹(√3/2) = π/6** (cosine branch [0, π]) and **sin⁻¹(1/2) = π/6** (sine branch [−π/2, π/2]). Sum: **π/6 + π/6 = π/3**. (This item bridges to inverse functions but is solved by the principal-value discipline established here.)
